Fairness metrics of a binary risk tool by group

Source: R/doss.R
fair.Rd

The confusion matrix of a risk score cut at cut within each group, and the usual rates computed from it: accuracy, sensitivity (true positive rate), specificity, false positive and false negative rates, positive and negative predictive values, the share and number predicted positive and the Matthews correlation, each with its ratio to the base group and, for the first eight, a Wilson score interval (Wilson 1927). A case is predicted positive when its score exceeds cut. No single metric defines fairness, and when base rates differ between groups the error rates and the predictive values cannot all be equal at once (Chouldechova 2017); the table shows which differ, not which should not.

Usage

fair(score, y, grp, cut = 0.5, base = 1, conf = 0.95)

Arguments

score

Risk scores: finite numbers, one per case.

y

Outcomes: 0 or 1 (or FALSE/TRUE), one per case.

grp

Group labels: numbers, text or a factor, one per case, no missing values. Groups are ordered as the factor's levels, or sorted.

cut

The cut: one number.

base

The group the ratios are taken against: its label, or its position from 1.

conf

The confidence level of the intervals, strictly between 0 and 1.

Value

A list of data frames, one row per group with its label in group: cnt (tp, fp, tn, fn, n), met (acc, tpr, tnr, fpr, fnr, ppv, npv, ppos, npos, mcc; NaN where a rate has an empty denominator), rat (each metric over the base group's), lo and hi (the interval ends of the first eight metrics; the last two columns NaN).

References

Wilson, E. B. (1927). Probable inference, the law of succession, and statistical inference. Journal of the American Statistical Association, 22(158), 209-212. doi:10.1080/01621459.1927.10502953

Chouldechova, A. (2017). Fair prediction with disparate impact: a study of bias in recidivism prediction instruments. Big Data, 5(2), 153-163. doi:10.1089/big.2016.0047

Examples

set.seed(1)
g <- rep(c("a", "b"), each = 100)
y <- rbinom(200, 1, ifelse(g == "a", 0.3, 0.5))
s <- plogis(rnorm(200, ifelse(y == 1, 0.8, -0.8)))
fair(s, y, g)$met
#>   group acc       tpr       tnr       fpr       fnr       ppv       npv ppos
#> 1     a 0.8 0.8125000 0.7941176 0.2058824 0.1875000 0.6500000 0.9000000 0.40
#> 2     b 0.8 0.8148148 0.7826087 0.2173913 0.1851852 0.8148148 0.7826087 0.54
#>   npos       mcc
#> 1   40 0.5776155
#> 2   54 0.5974235
